audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for elder care, Abishag's agency and consent, succession secrecy, Bathsheba's survival risk, royal anointing, sanctuary, and threatened execution.

verses.restored: King David was old, advanced in days. They covered him with garments, but he could not become warm.
His servants said, Let them seek for my lord the king a young virgin. Let her stand before the king, care for him, and lie in your embrace, so my lord the king may become warm.
They sought a beautiful young woman throughout all territory of Israel and found Abishag the Shunammite, and brought her to the king.
The young woman was exceedingly beautiful. She cared for the king and served him, but the king did not know her sexually.
Adonijah son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, I will be king. He prepared chariots, riders, and fifty men running before him.
His father had never grieved/challenged him by saying, Why have you done this? He also was very good in appearance, and his mother bore him after Absalom.
He conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and Abiathar the priest, and they supported Adonijah.
But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David's warriors were not with Adonijah.
Adonijah sacrificed sheep, cattle, and fattened animals by stone of Zoheleth beside En-rogel. He invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all men of Judah serving the king.
But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the warriors, or Solomon his brother.
Nathan spoke to Bathsheba, mother of Solomon: Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, while David our lord does not know?
Now come, please let me counsel you, so you may rescue your life and life of your son Solomon.
Go to King David and say: Did you not swear to your maidservant, Solomon your son shall reign after me and sit upon my throne? Why then has Adonijah become king?
Look, while you are still speaking there with the king, I will come after you and confirm your words.
Bathsheba went to the king in the chamber. The king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was serving the king.
Bathsheba bowed and prostrated herself before the king. The king said, What is yours/what do you seek?
She said, My lord, you swore by YHWH your Divine to your maidservant: Solomon your son shall reign after me and sit upon my throne.
Now, look, Adonijah has become king, and now, my lord the king, you do not know it.
He sacrificed cattle, fattened animals, and sheep in abundance, and invited all sons of the king, Abiathar the priest, and Joab commander of army, but Solomon your servant he did not invite.
You, my lord the king—the eyes of all Israel are upon you to tell them who shall sit upon throne of my lord the king after him.
Otherwise, when my lord the king lies with his ancestors, I and my son Solomon will be counted offenders.
Look, while she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet came.
They told the king, Look, Nathan the prophet. He came before the king and bowed on his face to ground.
Nathan said, My lord the king, did you say, Adonijah shall reign after me and sit upon my throne?

For he went down this day and sacrificed cattle, fattened animals, and sheep in abundance. He invited all sons of the king, commanders of army, and Abiathar the priest. Look, they eat and drink before him and say, Long live King Adonijah.
But me your servant, Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and Solomon your servant he did not invite.
Was this matter done by my lord the king without making known to your servants who should sit upon throne of my lord the king after him?
King David answered, Call Bathsheba to me. She came before the king and stood before him.
The king swore: As YHWH lives, who redeemed my life from all distress,
as I swore to you by YHWH, Divine of Israel, Solomon your son shall reign after me and sit upon my throne in my place—so I will do this day.
Bathsheba bowed with face to earth and prostrated before the king, saying, May my lord King David live forever.
King David said, Call Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada. They came before the king.
The king said, Take with you servants of your lord, cause Solomon my son to ride upon my mule, and bring him down to Gihon.
Let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him there as king over Israel. Blow trumpet and say, Long live King Solomon.
Come up after him, and he shall come and sit upon my throne. He shall reign in my place, and I appointed him leader over Israel and Judah.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada answered the king, Amen. Thus may YHWH, Divine of my lord the king, say.
As YHWH was with my lord the king, so may YHWH be with Solomon and make his throne greater than throne of my lord King David.
Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Cherethites, and Pelethites went down. They caused Solomon to ride upon King David's mule and brought him to Gihon.
Zadok the priest took horn of oil from tent and anointed Solomon. They blew trumpet, and all people said, Long live King Solomon.
All people came up after him, playing pipes and rejoicing with great joy, so earth split with their sound.
Adonijah and all guests with him heard it as they finished eating. Joab heard sound of trumpet and said, Why is city roaring?
While he was still speaking, look, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest came. Adonijah said, Come, for you are a worthy man and bring good news.
Jonathan answered Adonijah, No—our lord King David has made Solomon king.
The king sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Cherethites, and Pelethites, and they caused him to ride upon king's mule.
Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him king at Gihon. They came up from there rejoicing, and city resounded. This is sound you heard.
Also Solomon has sat upon throne of kingdom.
Moreover king's servants came to bless our lord King David, saying, May Divine make name of Solomon better than your name and his throne greater than your throne. The king bowed upon bed.
The king also said, Blessed be YHWH, Divine of Israel, who has given one to sit upon my throne this day while my eyes see it.
All guests who were with Adonijah trembled, arose, and each went his way.
Adonijah feared Solomon, arose, went, and grasped horns of altar.
It was told Solomon: Look, Adonijah fears King Solomon and has grasped horns of altar, saying, Let King Solomon swear to me this day that he will not kill his servant with sword.
Solomon said, If he becomes a worthy man, not one hair of him shall fall to earth; but if evil is found in him, he shall die.
King Solomon sent, and they brought him down from altar. He came and bowed to King Solomon, and Solomon said to him, Go to your house.

translation_notes: Abishag is a young woman selected across the kingdom for intimate elder care. The text records that David did not have sex with her, but it does not record her consent to recruitment, transport, bodily proximity, or service.
David's aging, inability to stay warm, and dependence do not diminish his human worth. Elder care must center consent, dignity, medical assessment, and the worker's safety.
Bathsheba and Solomon face credible lethal risk in a contested succession. Her coordinated testimony with Nathan occurs under survival pressure.
Adonijah's appearance, birth order, entourage, sacrifices, and elite supporters do not establish a right to rule.
Public acclamation and prophetic-priestly anointing do not make Solomon morally infallible or exempt him from later accountability.
The altar functions as claimed sanctuary, but Solomon's promise remains conditional and vague. Sacred space requires transparent protection, not discretionary royal mercy.
Women, servants, runners, animal handlers, musicians, guards, and residents absorb the labor and danger of elite succession but receive little narrative voice.
safety_note: Do not use this chapter to endorse sexualized caregiving, forced service by young women, dynastic entitlement, secret succession, leader worship, or discretionary execution. Abishag and Bathsheba are persons navigating royal systems, not instruments for male legitimacy.
